questions.stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: $29$ has exactly two factors: $1$ and $29$. $1$ is not prime (it has only one factor), $9 = 3 \times 3$, and $51 = 3 \times 17$.

questions.stem: What are all the factors of $18$?
questions.explanation: The factors of $18$ are all numbers that divide into $18$ exactly: $1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18$.

questions.stem: Express $60$ as a product of its prime factors.
questions.explanation: $60 = 2 \times 30 = 2 \times 2 \times 15 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 5 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5$. The other options include composite numbers like $10$, $30$, or $4$.
